hyps.why: When edge 1 is absent, edge 2 is the only route into node 2, so its quality matters more.
A strong direct conv path 0->3 compensates for the weakened edge 5.
Pooling after an identity feeder costs less because little learned content is smoothed away.
A skip bypass helps more when the other output feeders are heavy convs.
Redundant identity paths into the output add little beyond the existing shortcut.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, the path through node 1 carries more of the signal, so improving edge 0 pays off more.
With the sibling edge 1 removed, node 1 is the main route to deeper paths, so edge 0 quality matters more.
If edge 4 is already absent, edge 0 only reaches the output through edges 2 and 5, so removing it costs more.
A sibling conv on edge 1 keeps an alternative deep path alive, softening the cost of removing edge 0.
Pooled upstream features are already smoothed and lossy, which limits what a following conv can add.
